learning_outcomes.text: Correctly and fluently manage the logarithmic units of power, gain, and attenuation used in communication systems.
Apply the fundamentals of time and frequency domain analysis to solve problems in communication systems.
Characterize information, both as a signal and as a stochastic process, to be transmitted by a communication system, as well as the disturbances that limit the performance of said system.
Describe and distinguish the functional blocks of analog and digital communication systems.
Obtain the fundamental parameters of analog and digital communication systems.
Understand the limitations and performance of different analog and digital modulation systems.
Appropriately evaluate the trade-off between bandwidth and power consumption to achieve a certain quality in a given configuration of an analog or digital communication system.
Assimilate the fundamentals of decision theory and signal space so that they can be applied to solve signal detection problems in digital communication systems.
Understand the main analog and digital modulation techniques to identify the most appropriate technique in a given transmission configuration.
Discuss and evaluate in a group the most appropriate analog and/or digital modulation technique under given operating conditions and restrictions.

Apply knowledge of the different technological alternatives for deploying communication systems to design systems at a functional level that meet certain a priori imposed requirements and performance.

syllabus_topics: Tools and useful parameters in digital communication systems
Signal and noise representation in signal space
Parameters related to error probability: Q, erf, erfc, Q_M
Approximate calculation of P_e for generic constellation
Power gain of one modulation versus another
Hartley-Shannon formula and Shannon channel capacity limit
Systems based on amplitude and/or phase modulations under Gaussian channel

Analysis of amplitude and/or phase modulations (PAM, QAM, PSK, QPSK, OQPSK and DPSK): temporal, spectral and signal space representation, error probability in Gaussian channel, spectral and power efficiency
Detection of amplitude and/or phase modulated signals in linear channel
Conditions for no ISI in Gaussian channel
Continuous-time and discrete-time systems for Gaussian channel
Parameters of interest and results for Gaussian channel
Continuous-time and discrete-time systems for linear channel
Systems based on spread spectrum modulations
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is the sum of the Theory Block (60%) and the Practical Block (40%). The Practical Block score is calculated from two projects, each contributing 20% to the final grade, and consisting of online questionnaires (6% of project grade), class participation (24% of project grade), and a practical exam (70% of project grade). For the extraordinary call, students can take a theory exam (60%) and a practical exam (40%), or take only the theory exam (60%) and retain their practical block score from the ordinary call. For differentiated evaluation, the theory exam constitutes 100% of the final grade, scaled to 10 points.
